Our Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday, and on behalf of the organising team I want to thank everyone who made it happen.

From 5 to 7 November, Seminar Hall 2 at the Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune, hosted 41 MSc and early PhD students from 9 states. We received 112 applications and selected participants based on a statement of purpose and one reference.

Thank you to our speakers:
Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad), for the lectures on the Mordell–Weil theorem
Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai), for the lectures on modular forms
Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków to take us through computations in Sage

One moment I'll remember: an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer's notes. She corrected it on the spot and thanked him in front of the whole room. That is exactly the kind of exchange we were hoping for.

Thank you to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for guiding us from the first proposal to the last session. Thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when a booking went wrong. And thank you to the six PhD students who worked as TAs and ran the problem sessions. That format worked really well, and we plan to keep it.

The school was supported by ₹2.4 lakh from the institute's Student Initiative Grant, which covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation participants. We're very grateful for it.

On Day 2 the power went out for almost two hours and every laptop died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards, and it turned out to be the best session of the three days.

Finally, thank you to all the participants for the questions, the arguments at the board and the energy. Small schools like this matter, especially for MSc students. At a big conference it's hard to put your hand up and ask a basic question. Here people asked them all day.

Slides and problem sheets will be up on the department website within two weeks. We'll share the link here once they're live.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, depending on funding. If it happens, we'd love to see many of you back.

– [Your name], with Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza
